summary: Nature 2025 paper (X. Landreau et al.): proposes pulley-like counterweight system in the Antechamber/Grand Gallery; argues ramp models have physics, length, and spiral-slowness problems.
content: No documents from Khufu's times explain how the pyramid was built. Generally accepted theories rely on construction-ramps with sledges pulled up the growing pyramid. Ramp models face three problems: (i) unfavorable physics (lifting force scales with sin of slope, friction with cos); (ii) large ramp length (~1.5 km) and absence of archaeological traces; (iii) slowness of spiral ramps (single-file, ~20 corners, blocks stalled). Paper proposes the Antechamber was a pulley-like system with counterweights sliding down ramps. Notes modern Egyptologists might agree the solution is yet to be found.
